spark_scene.description: True-color view of the main Hawaiian Islands from northwestern islands to the large island in the southeast, with scattered white cumulus and elongated cloud bands over dark ocean and a thin gray veil over the ocean southwest of the central islands.

plumes.label: thin gray streak southwest of central islands
plumes.visual_description: thin translucent pale gray veil over dark ocean extending southwest from near the central islands, distinct from brighter white cumulus and cirrus

context.case_note: Mauna Loa NE rift eruption (Nov 27-Dec 10 2022); Kīlauea summit was also erupting until Dec 9 2022

volcano_status.source: USGS Hawaiian Volcano Observatory notices via HANS public API (https://volcanoes.usgs.gov/hans-public/api/search/search)

kilauea.activity_summary: The summit eruption of Kīlauea Volcano, within Halemaʻumaʻu crater, continued over the past 24 hours. All recent eruptive activity has been confined to the crater. No significant changes have been observed at the summit or in either rift zone.

mauna_loa.activity_summary: The Northeast Rift Zone eruption of Mauna Loa continues, with two active fissures feeding lava flows downslope. Fissure 3 remains the dominant source of the largest lava flow. The fissure 3 lava flows are traveling to the north toward the Daniel K.

result.caveats: Segmentation faint with low sam_confidence 0.45; Big Island source region is cloud-covered so continuity to vent cannot be verified; near-summit FIRMS clusters are lava from ongoing Mauna Loa NE rift eruption, not wildfires; light winds 6-17 kmh limit transport inference.
evidence: thin translucent pale gray veil over ocean SW of central islands, distinct from bright white textured cumulus/cirrus - not classic cloud, not brown smoke
both volcanoes officially erupting on 2022-12-01: Kilauea WATCH ORANGE erupting yes in Halema'uma'u, Mauna Loa WARNING RED erupting yes with NE rift fissures - vog plausible
plume upwind end 335.7 km from Mauna Loa summit and 367.8 km from Kilauea summit, no continuous trail from vent; source gap breaks vog geometry criterion
nearest non-volcanic fire Honolulu cluster n=21 at 18.7 km upwind, nearest_summit_km 344.1, but 21-pixel fire too small to confidently explain 10300 km2 236-km plume
10m wind at plume site from 351 deg at 7.3 kmh (northerly to southerly) broadly consistent with SW extension but too light/variable for firm attribution
